summary: Pixel-for-pixel the same rainbow Sierpinski fractal — geometry, palette and brightness all match — but the port's animation clock runs exactly 2.00x too fast, so orig(t) equals port(t/2) over the whole 120 s timeline tested.
observations: Rig: grid 16x16 (256 px), both sides. Both compile and run clean — no compileError/runtimeError on either side in any of the 14 runs. wantsSensors=false both sides; sensors feed irrelevant.

Both sides draw the same thing: a blocky Sierpinski / bit-AND fractal on the grid (large solid quadrants subdividing into the classic half-scale triangular self-similar blocks), coloured by a rainbow that walks continuously. Per-frame distinct-colour count is identical at matched phase (14/14 at t=0, 15/15, 12/12, 15/15, 15/15, 14/14 at orig t=0,2,4,6,8,10).

HEADLINE: the port runs at exactly double speed. A time-rescale fit corr(orig[t], port[a*t+b]) over 241 dumped frames (0-12 s @ 20 fps, default rig) peaks at a=0.500, b=-0.025 s with MEAN correlation 0.9967 across the whole window; per-frame best-match port times track orig/2 to the dump resolution (orig 1.0->port 0.45, 2.0->0.95, 4.0->1.95, 8.0->4.00, 12.0->5.95).

Matched-phase agreement is essentially exact: mean absolute per-channel pixel difference between orig(t) and port(t/2 - 0.025 s) is 2.43/255 over 12 s (worst frame 9.37, which is time-quantisation residual at a 2x rate). Same-time (unshifted) difference is 67.99/255 — i.e. the sides look completely unrelated frame-by-frame purely because of the speed error.

The 2x factor is constant, not drifting: at orig t=100 s the best-matching port frame is t=49.95 s (mean|diff| 3.14) and at orig t=120 s it is t=59.95 s (mean|diff| 4.73). Same-time diffs there are 96.79 and 69.81.

Independent confirmation from period autocorrelation of meanBrightness over a 125 s / 20 fps run: orig's first strong non-trivial peak is at lag 131 frames = 6.55 s; port's is at lag 65-66 frames = 3.25-3.30 s (and its harmonic at 197 frames). Ratio 2.00.

motion stat ratio is a constant ~2.08x at every frame rate tested: 5 fps orig 18.5 / port 35.1; 10 fps orig 9 / port 19; 20 fps orig 4.5 / port 9.4; 40 fps orig 2 / port 5; 2 fps orig 43 / port 66. motionLit tracks motion (dense pattern, ~50% duty) so no sparseness correction needed.

NEITHER side is frame-rate coupled — this is a pure speed-constant bug, not an fps/delta-time bug. Rendering the same side at 10 fps and 40 fps and comparing at absolute times gives mean|diff| 0.00 for BOTH orig and port once a constant 0.075 s frame-grid offset is applied (scan: off=+0.075 -> orig 0.00, port 0.00; off=0 -> orig 7.02, port 13.68). The port/orig factor fit is 0.495 at 10 fps and 0.495 at 40 fps — identical to the 20 fps fit.

No modes or regimes on either side. A 240 s / 2 fps survey rhythm image is homogeneous top-to-bottom for both sides — continuous hue walk plus fractal subdivision, no boundaries, no dark gaps, no super-cycle. The port's rhythm image has the same texture with visibly finer horizontal banding (2x rate), which is the only difference visible at survey scale.

Steady state is healthy on both sides. --skip 120 --seconds 12 @ 20 fps: orig brightnessTrend steady, zeroMotionFrames 0, meanBrightness avg 47.8 (min 15 max 109); port steady, zeroMotionFrames 0, avg 50.5 (min 13 max 103). --seconds 30 --fps 4: orig avg 54.1 / port 51.6, both steady. No decay, no freeze, no saturation on either side.

Brightness envelopes are statistically identical over a long window despite the speed error: baseline (6 s @ 20 fps) orig meanBrightness avg 54.1 min 14 max 104, port avg 54.4 min 14 max 104. The port is not brighter or dimmer, just faster.

Resolution behaviour matches: re-rendered at --grid 8x8 and --grid 48x48, both sides rasterize at native grid resolution (48x48 shows many more, finer self-similar blocks than 16x16 on BOTH sides) rather than drawing into a fixed logical canvas. The motion ratio stays 5:9 at 8x8, 5:9 at 48x48 — the 2x is a global time constant, not resolution-dependent.
Both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent: --seed 1234 produces byte-identical per-frame stats series to --seed 1 on both orig and port.

Frame-to-frame filmstrips (baseline, 3.00-3.55 s) show the same character of motion on both sides — a Sierpinski block growing/subdividing smoothly with a simultaneous hue slide, no jitter or jumping on either side. The port simply covers about twice as much of that evolution in the same 12 frames.
CONTROL SURFACE: both sides expose ZERO settable controls (probe table reports '(no settable controls)' for orig and for port). No control-surface mismatch.
feedback: The port's animation is exactly 2.00x too fast — halve whatever time/phase increment drives the pattern. This is the only defect found; fix it and the port should be indistinguishable. Concretely: orig(t) == port(t/2) to within 2.4/255 mean absolute pixel error across a 12 s window, and the relation still holds exactly at t=100 s and t=120 s, so it is a single constant, not a drift or an accumulator error.

Target numbers to verify a fix against (default 16x16 grid rig, seed 1, 20 fps): the original's meanBrightness autocorrelation has its first strong peak at lag 131 frames = 6.55 s; the port currently peaks at 65-66 frames = 3.27 s. After the fix the port's peak should land at 131 frames.

Second check for a fix: the `motion` stat at 20 fps should drop from ~9.4 to ~4.5 (5 fps: 35.1 -> 18.5; 40 fps: 5 -> 2), and the same-time mean absolute pixel difference against the original over 0-12 s should drop from ~68/255 to near 0.

Do NOT change anything else. Geometry (the bit-AND Sierpinski subdivision), the rainbow palette, per-frame colour count, brightness min/avg/max, resolution-dependent rasterization, steady-state stability and seed-independence all already match the original exactly at matched phase.

This is not a delta-time/frame-rate bug — both sides are already perfectly fps-invariant (10 fps and 40 fps renders of each side are byte-identical at equal absolute times). So the fix belongs in a literal speed constant, not in how elapsed time is accumulated.
